The PostHog wizard, split into store, agent, and tui

A report on the refactor stack from main (v2.76.0) to posthog/split-p6-run-store: what the process looks like now, why it is shaped that way, how each claim was verified, and what is left. Generated 2026-09-20 from the branch, the PR comments, and the real-run artefacts.

Summary

OutcomeOne package, one process, three surfaces plus a composition root: src/store (state and every contract), src/agent (one run), src/tui (rendering), src/cli (argv and wiring). Cross-surface imports go through eight public entries; the compiler, an architecture test suite, and a bundle audit all enforce the same matrix. New capabilityA control API over a unix socket mirrors the store, so CI, a snapshot route, and coding agents drive the real TUI or the headless surface without a keyboard. Every parent-side tool is now a socket client; the old in-process host is gone. On the headless surface one POST /runs is one agent run alone. Store modelA RunStore is the state of one agent run. FlowStore chains runs: flow, gates, interrupts, the session every run inherits, and the artefacts runs create. The task stream publishes one run store. BehaviourGoldens from main stay byte identical (frames, flow traces, analytics sequences, decision traces). Real runs of all nine profiled programs reproduce the previous screen paths; the two composed-flow diffs that appeared were one regression (fixed, re-run) and one intended change (documented). Size973 files changed from main, +22,557 / −8,561 lines across 23 commits in seven stacked draft PRs. Tests on the P6 commit: 213 files, 3259 tests, all passed. StatusEvery branch is signed and pushed. Seven stacked draft PRs are open (P0 to P7, the last two as #1282 and #1283), the nine-program PNG gallery is on #1278, and CI plus the workbench snapshot suite are running against the stack head.

How to read this report

Diagrams are arranged as a zoom, following the C4 model's ladder and arc42's separation of static structure, runtime behaviour, and deployment. Each level answers a different question and is drawn for a different reader; no diagram mixes levels.

Every figure states its purpose and its key. Element types are in brackets, arrows point from caller to callee and carry a verb and, between processes, the protocol. Colours mean the same on every diagram:

Checklist applied to each figure: title with type and scope, key, every element named and typed with a short description, technology where it matters, every line one-directional and labelled, under twenty elements, consistent colours. Sources for these rules are listed at the end.

What happened, in order

  1. Plan approved (2026-09-18). Three surfaces with exact names, a cli composition root, an optional control server owned by the store, one release, baselines from main kept byte identical, a test harness per surface. The plan rejected extra layers (shared, app, host) and required every cross-surface edge to be soft: a types file, a barrel, an injected instance.
  2. P0 to P2. Test scaffold and goldens captured on main; the agent given a run contract (ProgramRunConfig) instead of the program config; flows registered into the store as data, presentation moved to the TUI, console renderers moved out of the store.
  3. P3. The tree moved with git mv into src/store, src/agent, src/tui, src/cli; every cross-surface import routed through barrels; tsc -b project references; per-surface Vitest projects with restricted aliases; the allowlist of known violations reached zero and was deleted.
  4. P4. A control API over a unix socket. First shipped with view types and derived status; then redesigned on request to be a store mirror: ControlState is the session whitelist plus the store atoms plus the legal actions, one setter per action, hooks only for what the store cannot do (credentials, detection, an agent run, exit).
  5. P5. The e2e harness became a socket client: launcher, pure decision function, client-side fixed loop, MCP proxy over HTTP, headless smoke script. The in-process host and its driver were deleted. Docs and skills rewritten for the socket contract.
  6. Reviews. Five independent review passes (architecture, code quality, tests, docs against the goal, idiom). Twenty-eight findings fixed in two commits (409 fences, abortable long polls, a real 413, socket path safety, param validation, redaction by word, per-run cleanups, launch words from program config, parity tests made strict). Ten items deliberately left and listed. Exceptions to the boundary named.
  7. Real runs. All nine profiled programs run through the snapshot route on the P5 stack; frames compared against the old host; PNG galleries rendered for the PRs. Diagrams redrawn three times on request: layered boxes, then Mermaid, then coloured with horizontal cards and intent-heavy text.
  8. Correction: the store is one agent run. The task stream is store level; a store is attached to a single agent run; the TUI, which chains runs, builds its flow and UI state on top. Chosen: refactor now, in this stack.
  9. P6. RunStore per agent run, WizardStore renamed FlowStore, startRun(session), per-run task streams, resetRunState removed. All gates green.
  10. Regression found by a real run. The self-driving outro lost its Dashboard and Notebook links: run 1 created them, run 2's fresh store reset them. Fixed by making the two URLs session artefacts on the flow. Both snapshot routes and the headless smoke re-run on the fixed commit; outro identical to P5 again.
  11. Blocked, then a reboot. Commit signing fails in 1Password; P4, P5, P6, and the asset branch wait unsigned. A reboot wiped the temporary tooling directory; the generator, scripts, and comment drafts were rebuilt under the workbench directory and the regenerated P4 and P5 diagrams came out byte identical to what is posted.
  12. P7: full store controls. The requirement: hook the control surface up with configs to run any agent without accounting for the flow. Verified that a skill-only run already worked through the generic program; the gaps were screen-gated writes and a run request that could not shape the run config. Shipped GET /store and POST /store/<setter> over a whitelist typed on the boundary list, and a data-field config overlay on POST /runs. Actions stay for keyboard parity.

Level 0: context

Two facts at this level drive everything below. First, the process is one Node program in a terminal; there is no server component of our own, so "surfaces" are source roots inside one process, not deployables. Second, a parent process can now stand where the developer stands: the socket carries the same commits a keyboard would, and the frame comes back through the same terminal.

[1] The full thingnpx @posthog/wizard [command]bin.ts preflight, @cli/main, dispatchProgram picks runWizard; startTUI builds the FlowStore; per flow step one startRun + runAgent, then completeRunStep. [2] A workflow, headlesswizard [command] --headless-DONOTUSE-EXPERIMENTAL --api-key … --project-id … --install-dir …dispatchProgram picks runWizardHeadless; run-non-interactive.ts builds a FlowStore with the same flow, installs HeadlessUI, runs ciPreRun or the onReady detection, one runAgent, outro to the log. [3] Just an agentin process: runAgent(runConfigFor(config), session) from @agent; over the socket: POST /runs { programId, installDir?, frameworkContext?, skillId? } on the headless surfaceone run: bootstrap, gates (resolved at once without a TUI), the sequence and harness the binding picks; writes back only through getUI(). Over the socket the hook does store.startRun on a fresh RunStore and calls runAgent(…, { composed: true }); the ledger records the result.agent and store; a WizardUI must be installed (cli/main.ts installs LoggingUI, startTUI installs StoreUI)
Does the control API run individual agents alone? Yes, on the headless surface: each POST /runs is one independent agent run on a fresh RunStore, with its own installDir, merged frameworkContext, and skillId; a second POST /runs while one is in flight is a 409, and GET /runs lists every run with its end state. On the TUI surface (--ci --control-socket) it does not: POST /run only releases the launched program's own run, and POST /runs answers 501 there.
Level 2: components
Level 3: objects and data ownership

How the TUI process spawns the stores, in order

  1. src/cli/runners/run-wizard.ts:136 calls startTUI(WIZARD_VERSION, config.id).
  2. src/tui/start-tui.ts:37 builds new FlowStore(flowFor(program).flow). The constructor (src/store/state/store.ts:125-130) derives the gates from the flow, creates a first idle RunStore from the initial session, and subscribes to it so every run commit re-emits as one flow commit.
  3. start-tui.ts:39 builds new UiStore(store); src/tui/ui-store.ts:25 subscribes to the FlowStore and derives the active screen, the nav direction, and the presentation atoms.
  4. start-tui.ts:41-42 builds new StoreUI(store) and installs it with setUI. Each WizardUI method is one FlowStore setter call (src/store/ui/store-ui.ts:31).
  5. start-tui.ts:44-46 renders App with { store, ui }. Screens read both and commit only through FlowStore setters. startTUI returns the FlowStore in its handle.
  6. run-wizard.ts:219, dev build with --control-socket only: attachControlServer(activeTui.store, { hooks }) mirrors the FlowStore.
  7. run-wizard.ts:272-291 defines beginRun: activeTui.store.startRun(runSession) (line 276) creates the RunStore for one agent run; new TaskStreamPush({ store: run, … }) (line 277) attaches to that RunStore (src/store/task-stream/task-stream-push.ts:180 subscribes).
  8. store.ts:162-170 is startRun: cancel a pending question and notice, unsubscribe the previous run, create new RunStore({ ...session, ...RUN_SESSION_DEFAULTS }), subscribe, emit once, return the run.
  9. run-wizard.ts:318 sends composed steps through advanceStep (lines 65-82): beginRun, then runAgent(…, run.session, { composed: true }), then store.completeRunStep(step.id) (store.ts:177-184 records the step and idles the run).
  10. run-wizard.ts:341-342 starts the main run the same way: beginRun, then runAgent(runConfigFor(config), run.session).
  11. The agent writes through getUI() only: StoreUI, then the FlowStore setter, then the delegated this._run setter (41 delegation sites), then RunStore emit, FlowStore emit, UiStore version bump, Ink re-render.
  12. Headless twin: src/cli/runners/run-non-interactive.ts:218 FlowStore, :226 StoreUI (controlled) or :228 HeadlessUI, :234 TaskStreamPush, :252 startRun, :302 attachControlServer, :421 runAgent. Each POST /runs goes through src/cli/control-hooks.ts:116 startRun and :122 runAgent.

The one rule of P6. A key belongs to the flow if a later run must see it (credentials, detection, setup flags, the dashboard and notebook a run created) and to the run if a later run must not see it (its phase, outro, questions, notices, tasks, status, token usage). store.session is the flow's map with the active run's keys laid over it, so screens and the control API did not change what they read.

Runtime scenarios

Four scenarios, chosen because each exercises a different seam: the interactive path, the composed path that motivated P6, the published control path, and the harness route that produced the evidence. Each lifeline is a block from the levels above.
Data flow and trust boundaries

What crosses the socket, and what never does

Leaves the process over the socketStays inside
version, currentScreen, tasks, statusMessages, eventPlan, handoffText, unanswered setupQuestions, legal actions; session reduced to 21 whitelisted keys plus hasCredentials and projectId; frameworkContext after redaction (secret:<id> refs become [secret-ref], secret-looking keys become [redacted]); outroData.errorDetail after sanitizeErrorDetail access token, personal API key, the API user record, every answer to an ask, the secret vault. Credentials reduce to a boolean. The result payload of a run records question ids and prompts, never an answer value.

The socket itself is created mode 0600 in a directory the parent owns; a stale socket file is replaced only if lstat says it is a socket, a live one is refused, the wizard unlinks it on exit. The personal key travels to the child in the environment, never in argv; outer agent credentials (CLAUDE*, ANTHROPIC*, AI_AGENT*) are stripped from the child's environment.

Builds and where runs execute

Interface contracts

The soft edges, one table each. Every table is what a reviewer needs to hold a surface to its promise; the code is the source of truth and the architecture suite pins the member lists.

WizardUI (src/store/ui/wizard-ui.ts)

44 methods plus readonly interactive: boolean. The agent's whole vocabulary toward whoever renders: status, spinners, tasks, token usage, outro, requestQuestion, showTaskNotice, waitForGate, waitForAiOptIn, onEnterScreen. StoreUI (interactive) commits to the FlowStore; LoggingUI and HeadlessUI print; NullUI is silent. The store owns getUI/setUI.

FlowStoreApi (src/store/state/store-api.ts)

Pick<FlowStore, StoreBoundaryMember> over 63 names. The architecture test derives the real usage of tui, cli, and the harness with the TypeScript checker and fails when the list drifts, so widening the boundary is an explicit edit. P6 added startRun and removed resetRunState.

RunAgent and ProgramRunConfig (src/agent/types.ts, src/store/agent-protocol)

runAgent(config, session, { composed? }) is one independent run. ProgramRunConfig carries exactly what the agent reads: id, run, agentFlow, skillId, requiresAi, seedTasks, report and event-plan files, audit ledger, stream workflow id, tool allow and deny lists, postAuthGateIds. runConfigFor(config) strips everything else; the agent never sees steps or screens.

Flow and FlowStep (src/store/state/flow.ts)

Flow { programId, skillId, steps }; FlowStep { id, label, screenId?, show?, isComplete?, gate?, onInit?, onReady?, controlActions? }. resolveActiveScreen(flow, session, interrupts) picks the screen; there is no imperative navigation. Flow keys: auth, run, outro, exit, mint-failure, mcp, slack-connect, keep-skills. Interrupts: settings-override, managed-settings, port-conflict, manual-auth-code, auth-error, session-timeout, wizard-ask, task-notice.

RunStateSource (src/store/task-stream/types.ts)

Pick<RunStore, 'session' | 'tasks' | 'eventPlan' | 'handoffText' | 'subscribe' | 'setEventPlan'>: what the task stream reads. Built per run by the runners and by the control hooks; attached before the agent starts; shut down after the run settles and before the ledger records the result.

ControlHooks (src/store/control/types.ts, implemented in src/cli/control-hooks.ts)

setCredentials(), detect(req), startRun(req), shutdown(). Only what the store cannot do itself. POST /run is not a hook: it is store.requestRun(), which the TUI runner waits on.

Control HTTP API (src/store/control/server.ts, ROUTES)

RouteBehaviour
GET /health{ ok, version, surface, pid, program }
GET /state{ ok, state }, the projection
GET /state?wait=<ms>&since=<version>long poll: resolves on the first commit with version > since, on timeout (capped at 10 min), or on close
POST /actions/<id> body { params }one action legal on the current screen, one store setter, params validated never coerced, returns the state
GET /storethe store setters a parent may call by name: name, description, params (P7)
POST /store/<setter> body { params }one whitelisted FlowStore setter, named params validated, on either surface whatever the screen; returns the state (P7)
POST /credentialsresolves the API key into project credentials and commits them (400 without a key, 409 while running)
POST /runTUI surface: requestRun, idempotent
POST /detect body { programId?, installDir? }headless surface: detection through the store's setters (409 while running)
POST /runs body { programId?, skillId?, installDir?, frameworkContext?, config? }headless surface: one independent run on a fresh RunStore; a skillId alone runs on the generic agent-skill program; config lays agentFlow, allowedTools, disallowedTools, requiresAi, reportFile, eventPlanFile, streamWorkflowId over the program (P7); 409 while one runs; 501 on the TUI surface
GET /runsthe ledger: runId, programId, skillId, installDir, status, error, startedAt, finishedAt, result (result = ControlState at run end)
POST /shutdownflush and exit, idempotent (409 while running)

Failures: 400 bad body or param or unknown action or program, 404 unknown route, 409 run in flight, 413 body over 64 KB, 415 not JSON, 500 hook failure, 501 the other surface's route.

Full store controls (P7)

StoreSetter.name is typed as a STORE_BOUNDARY_MEMBERS entry, so the wire can reach exactly what the TUI, the cli, and the harness may reach and nothing more; the compiler rejected setSkillId for that reason. The table in src/store/control/setters.ts holds 25 setters: setup (completeSetup, grantSharing, declineSharing, setDetectionComplete, setDetectedFramework), session (setCredentials, setRoleAtOrganization, setFrameworkConfig, setFrameworkContext, setIntegrate, enableFeature, addDiscoveredFeature, switchProgram), follow-ups (setMcpComplete, setSkillsComplete, setMcpSuggestedPromptsDismissed, setSlackStepDismissed, setSlackConnected, setGithubConnected, confirmSelfDrivingHandoff, setOutroDismissed, setMintHandoff), and interrupts (resolvePendingQuestion, resolveTaskNotice, dismissOutage). Run atoms and setters with effects beyond the store stay off the wire. A run request's config lays data fields over the program before runConfigFor picks what the agent reads; functions in a run recipe never cross the wire.

Decisions and why

DecisionWhyConsequence
Exactly three surfaces plus src/cli; anything else needs a stated reasonthe first plan invented layers (shared, programs, app, host) that blurred ownershipevery new concern goes into the narrowest existing surface; the cli holds only parsing, surface choice, and forwarding
Soft edges only: a types file, a barrel, an injected instance; deep imports fail at three levelsa boundary that is enforced in one place drifts in the otherstsc -b, the architecture suite, and the bundle audit all encode the same matrix
Flows are data, the screen is resolved from state, gates latchno imperative navigation, so a socket commit and a keystroke are indistinguishable to the renderkeyboard equivalence is testable per (screen, action) pair
Control API is a store mirror: session whitelist, atoms, legal actions; one setter per action; hooks only for auth, detection, a run, exitthe first design carried view types and derived status; the request was an extremely minimal API tightly coupled to the store shapethe wire cannot say anything the store does not; RunRecord.result is that state at run end
HTTP/1.1 over a 0600 unix socket, JSON, long poll on the versionlocal, permissioned by the filesystem, trivial from curl or any languageno ports, no auth layer of our own, a parent owns the directory
The harness is a socket client; picks are computed client sidethe in-process host mirrored the runner by hand and driftedthe CI route, the MCP route, and the smoke share one launcher and one decision function
A store is one agent run; the flow chains runs above it; the task stream publishes one run storethe correction that the store attaches to a single agent run and the TUI builds its flow state on topRunStore, FlowStore.startRun, per-run streams; resetRunState gone
Dashboard and notebook URLs are session artefacts on the flowa real self-driving run lost the outro links when run 2 reset themlater runs and the outro inherit them; a headless ledger record for a later run also carries them
Run 2 of a composed flow starts with an empty status logthe log is one run's state; the old behaviour showed run 1's tail until run 2 spokeone intended frame diff against P5, documented
Goldens from main stay byte identical; real snapshot cadence per phasea refactor must not change what users seeevery phase compared screen paths and transition frames; progress frames vary by timing and are reviewed, not diffed

Glossary

surfaceone of the three source roots (store, agent, tui) with its own types file, barrel, tsconfig, Vitest project, README
public entry, barrelthe only import targets across surfaces: index.ts, types.ts, and the named secondary barrels
flow, flow keya program's screens as data; the key is an opaque string the TUI maps to a component and analytics uses as the screen name
gatea promise per gated step that resolves once and stays resolved
interruptan overlay screen raised by state (ask, notice, auth error); LIFO
FlowStorethe flow, gates, interrupts, cross-run session, and the active run; formerly WizardStore
RunStorethe state of one agent run
UiStorepresentation state derived from the FlowStore per commit
WizardUI, StoreUIthe interface the agent calls; the implementation that turns calls into store commits
control socket, ControlStatethe unix-socket HTTP API and the projection it serves
ledgerthe record of independent runs started over the socket
route (harness)one way of driving the wizard from outside: snapshot, MCP, headless smoke
profilea program's scripted decision policy for the fixed loop
goldena committed expected output the tests compare against byte for byte
chunk manifestwhich source module groups land in which built chunk and what each imports
